blindSummary:
This country is safe in practice but thin in law for trans visitors. Same-sex relations are legal and discrimination based on sexual orientation is banned, but gender identity, gender expression, and sex characteristics are not included in any anti-discrimination legislation, and there is no legal gender recognition law. These are resident-facing gaps: a visitor faces no legal exposure.

It is a very small, very low-crime country closely integrated with a larger neighbouring state; there is no documented pattern of anti-trans violence, no bathroom law, and no border friction (entry runs through the region's passport-free area via those neighbours). Social attitudes are conservative but not mobilised-hostile.
blindOutOfScope: Anti-discrimination and legal-gender-recognition gaps are resident-facing.
blindLocalsOnly: No legal gender recognition law and no gender-identity anti-discrimination coverage — resident-facing gaps.
blindSourceSummaries: International LGBT-rights organisation country overview (updated March 2026): mixed situation - same-sex relations legal and sexual-orientation discrimination banned, but gender identity/expression/sex characteristics not covered by any anti-discrimination law; no legal gender marker change; surgeries on intersex children are not prohibited; marriage and joint adoption available since January 2025; there is an official state religion whose senior national religious leader publicly opposed marriage equality; first Pride held in 2022.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 401); the underlying news-agency feature covers very small states in this region playing catch-up on LGBT equality, including this country.

Regional news outlet (May 2022): a neighbouring state moving to lower hurdles for LGBT citizens to donate blood - regional context relevant to this country, which is closely integrated with that neighbour (page largely navigation content at fetch time).

LGBT travel-news archive article on gay life in this country (March 2012): with a population of about 35,000 there is no organised gay scene - friendship networks are the scene; it notes few organised opponents of gay people - no religious extremists, no far-right groups, no politicians demanding homophobic laws; gay people live comfortably with little interference.

Magazine (Jan 2016): the country's hereditary ruler called rainbow families irresponsible in a new-year interview, said children have a right to a normal family, and suggested the country could ignore an adverse ruling by a regional human-rights court; a local LGBT organisation said it was shocked; an opposition party called the remarks contrary to the constitution and to that court's convention.

Motion in the national legislature (Sept 2022): an MPs' motion to open civil marriage to all regardless of gender and sexual orientation, removing all remaining legal differences; it notes registered partnerships are widely seen as a second-class form of marriage, and that the hereditary ruler had said in 2021 he had nothing against marriage equality except adoption.
